rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes alloying with Al or Cr to form an oxide scale, whereas the target uses liquid-metal dealloying in molten Cu to create a bicontinuous RHEA–Cu composite. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies isothermal exposure at 1000 °C in air, while the target involves vacuum-sealed reaction in molten Cu at 1200 °C and thermal conductivity measurement up to ~800 °C. The regimes are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes selective oxidation forming a protective oxide scale, whereas the target relies on preferential dissolution of Ti into Cu, retention of W/Ta/V as ligaments, and formation of a W-rich interlayer. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower mass gain and slower degradation (oxidation resistance), while the target predicts and measures enhanced thermal conductivity and reduced He-induced swelling. The properties and directions are unrelated.
